title: Two Men Died Over a Roll of Duct Tape
tested_variable: baseline (cut 2: story rebuilt around the mechanism and the shortcut)

source.publisher: U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board (CSB)
source.title: Case Study: Confined Space Entry - Worker and Would-be Rescuer Asphyxiated. Valero Energy Corporation Refinery, Delaware City, DE, November 5, 2005

beats.narration: This reactor is full of the same gas you're breathing right now.

claims.claim: Nitrogen is 78 percent of the air we breathe.
claims.quote: Nitrogen, which makes up 78 percent of the air we breathe, is non-toxic

claims.claim: The reactor was nitrogen-filled.
claims.quote: Nobody saw him enter the nitrogen-filled reactor

beats.narration: One or two breaths of it, and you're unconscious. No warning.

claims.claim: Collapse comes within one or two breaths.
claims.quote: he would collapse from a lack of oxygen within one or two breaths

claims.claim: Loss of consciousness follows one or two breaths.
claims.quote: After only one or two breaths the oxygen concentration in the blood drops dangerously low, and the victim is likely to lose consciousness in less than 60 seconds

claims.claim: There is no warning.
claims.quote: overcomes the victim without warning

beats.narration: It killed two experienced men. One of them taught safety training.

claims.claim: Two men died.
claims.quote: asphyxiation death of two contractor employees

claims.claim: Both were experienced; the foreman had taught hazard awareness.
claims.quote: The first victim had nearly ten years experience working in refineries; the second had more than 25, and had provided hazard awareness training to many co-workers throughout his career

beats.narration: November 2005, a Delaware refinery. A night crew has to bolt a pipe back onto this reactor before the shift ends.

claims.claim: Date.
claims.quote: November 5, 2005, nitrogen asphyxiation death of two

claims.claim: Place.
claims.quote: refinery in Delaware City, Delaware

claims.claim: Night-shift crew.
claims.quote: Matrix nightshift boilermaker crew

claims.claim: The job was to reassemble a pipe on the vessel.
claims.quote: preparing to reassemble a pipe on a pressure vessel

claims.claim: Bolting.
claims.quote: reinstalling the stud nuts and washers

claims.claim: Management wanted it sealed before the end of the night shift.
claims.quote: management wanted the pipe installation work completed and the reactor sealed before the end of the night shift

beats.narration: Then someone spots a roll of duct tape, five feet down inside. It can't stay there.

claims.claim: A pipefitter pointed out the tape.
claims.quote: a Matrix pipefitter told them that a roll of duct tape was lying on the

claims.claim: About five feet below the opening.
claims.quote: about five feet below the opening

claims.claim: It could not be left inside.
claims.quote: reactor cleanliness criteria prohibited leaving the tape inside the reactor

beats.narration: The right way means a trained crew, a permit, and a delay. The fast way is a piece of wire, bent into a hook. It looks like nothing.

claims.claim: Entry needed a trained crew and a permit.
claims.quote: knew entry would require a specially trained and equipped crew and confined space

claims.claim: That meant a delay, possibly past the end of the shift.
claims.quote: which would delay their work, possibly beyond the end of their work shift

claims.claim: They chose a wire hook instead.
claims.quote: they decided to make a long wire hook

claims.claim: The only warning on the manway was red tape.
claims.quote: the red tape was the only warning on the manway

beats.narration: Here's what they're actually standing over. The reactor was just loaded with new catalyst that can't touch oxygen.

claims.claim: The reactor had just been loaded with new catalyst.
claims.quote: finished loading the reactor with the new catalyst

claims.claim: The catalyst had to be protected from oxygen.
claims.quote: protect the newly loaded catalyst from reacting with oxygen in the air

beats.narration: So it's been pumped full of nitrogen, on purpose. And that nitrogen is drifting out of the manway they're working at.

claims.claim: Purging means pumping in nitrogen to remove oxygen.
claims.quote: Purging is the process of pumping inert gas, such as nitrogen, into pressure vessels, pipes, and other equipment to remove oxygen or other hazardous gases

claims.claim: The purge was a deliberate step of the catalyst loading procedure.
claims.quote: as part of the catalyst loading procedure

claims.claim: The nitrogen was venting out through the manway.
claims.quote: The nitrogen purge gas was slowly venting out of the reactor through the manway

claims.claim: It vented onto the work platform.
claims.quote: the reactor was on a nitrogen purge that vented directly onto the work platform area

beats.narration: Nitrogen isn't poison. It's most of the air. But your urge to breathe comes from carbon dioxide building up, not from oxygen running out.

claims.claim: Nitrogen is non-toxic and most of the air.
claims.quote: Nitrogen, which makes up 78 percent of the air we breathe, is non-toxic

claims.claim: The breathing reflex is driven by carbon dioxide, not by lack of oxygen.
claims.quote: The breathing reflex is controlled primarily by the amount of carbon dioxide in the blood rather than the shortage of oxygen

beats.narration: So your body raises no alarm. It can simply stop breathing.

claims.claim: Nitrogen gives no stimulus.
claims.quote: nitrogen, which is odorless, tasteless, and colorless, provides no stimulus

claims.claim: The body may simply stop breathing.
claims.quote: body may simply stop breathing, as carbon dioxide accumulation in the blood is insufficient to stimulate the breathing reflex

beats.narration: Their permit doesn't mention nitrogen. There's no warning sign. And their training covered the danger inside a tank, not the air above the opening.

claims.claim: The permit did not tell them about the purge.
claims.quote: safe work permit did not inform them that the reactor was on nitrogen purge

claims.claim: No nitrogen warning sign was in place.
claims.quote: a nitrogen purge warning sign and barricade were not in place in the work area

claims.claim: Training did not cover an oxygen-deficient atmosphere outside the opening.
claims.quote: their training did not address the possibility that an oxygen-deficient atmosphere might be present outside the confined space near the access opening

claims.claim: Training did cover the hazard inside a confined space.
claims.quote: confined space training that addressed the confined space nitrogen asphyxiation hazard

beats.narration: The first man tries the hook standing. Then kneeling. Then, investigators believe, he sits on the rim, with his legs inside.

claims.claim: Standing, then kneeling.
claims.quote: He tried from a standing position next to the manway and then, apparently to get closer, tried kneeling on the platform next to the manway

claims.claim: CSB's conclusion: he likely sat on the ledge.
claims.quote: the CSB concluded that the first victim likely stepped over the manway studs and then sat on the narrow ledge

claims.claim: Legs inside the reactor.
claims.quote: sat down, and dangled his legs inside the reactor

claims.claim: Nobody saw him enter; fell or went in on purpose is unknown.
claims.quote: Nobody saw him enter the nitrogen-filled reactor, but he either fell in or intentionally went into the reactor

beats.narration: His foreman grabs a ladder and climbs down to save him. A few breaths later, he's down too.

claims.claim: The foreman grabbed a ladder and climbed in.
claims.quote: the foreman grabbed a nearby ladder, shoved it down the manway, and quickly climbed in the reactor

claims.claim: He was attempting a rescue.
claims.quote: His co-worker, the crew foreman, was asphyxiated while attempting to rescue him

claims.claim: He succumbed within a few breaths.
claims.quote: Within a few breaths the foreman was the second victim to succumb to oxygen deprivation

beats.narration: A third man reaches the ladder. He stops. He gets on the radio.

claims.claim: The contract administrator approached, hesitated, radioed.
claims.quote: saw the nightshift contract administrator approach the ladder, hesitate, and then heard him urgently call for help on his radio

claims.claim: That was the trained response.
claims.quote: he would have immediately announced the emergency on the radio and remained on the platform, safely away from the manway until qualified emergency response personnel arrived

beats.narration: Nobody takes a shortcut thinking it's the one that kills them.

claims.claim: People are caught off guard by this hazard.
claims.quote: hazard of asphyxiation was not expected and personnel were typically caught off guard

claims.claim: Experience and training were overwhelmed in the moment.
claims.quote: overwhelmed his refinery work experience, safety training, and proper emergency response protocols

beats.narration: If a vessel is being purged, the opening itself is the danger. And if someone goes down: stay out, and call.

claims.claim: The air outside the opening can be oxygen-deficient.
claims.quote: An oxygen-deficient atmosphere might exist outside a confined space opening

claims.claim: Only trained, equipped people should attempt a rescue.
claims.quote: Only qualified and trained personnel equipped with the necessary safety equipment should attempt a rescue

beats.narration: Two men never came home. We tell their story so no other family goes through this.

claims.claim: Both men died.
claims.quote: transported to the hospital where they were pronounced dead

claims.claim: Two died.
claims.quote: asphyxiation death of two contractor employees
